title: Attention Is All You Need
authors:

  Jones, Aidan N. Gomez, Lukasz Kaiser, Illia Polosukhin
reason: Introduced the Transformer architecture, which replaced RNNs/CNNs and defines the current state-of-the-art era of NMT.
summary: Existing sequence transduction models rely on complex recurrent or convolutional neural networks that are difficult to parallelize. The authors propose the Transformer, a new architecture based solely on attention mechanisms that eliminates recurrence and convolutions. The model achieved a state-of-the-art 28.4 BLEU on English-to-German translation and 41.8 BLEU on English-to-French translation while requiring significantly less training time.

title: Neural Machine Translation of Rare Words with Subword Units
authors: Rico Sennrich, Barry Haddow and Alexandra Birch
reason: Introduced subword units (BPE), a fundamental component used in almost all modern NMT and Transformer-based systems to handle vocabulary.
summary: To address the problem of out-of-vocabulary words in neural machine translation, this paper proposes encoding rare and unknown words as sequences of subword units rather than relying on a fixed vocabulary or dictionary back-off. By using segmentation techniques like byte pair encoding, the method allows the model to translate names, compounds, and cognates through their smaller constituent parts. This approach improved translation performance on WMT 15 tasks, increasing scores by 1.1 BLEU for English-German and 1.3 BLEU for English-Russian.

title: Neural Machine Translation by Jointly Learning to Align and Translate
authors: Dzmitry Bahdanau and Kyunghyun Cho and Yoshua Bengio
reason: Introduced the attention mechanism in NMT, which solved the fixed-length vector bottleneck and is the direct precursor to the Transformer architecture.
summary: Traditional encoder-decoder models struggle with performance because they compress an entire source sentence into a single fixed-length vector. This paper proposes an attention mechanism that allows the model to automatically search for relevant parts of the source sentence when predicting each target word. This approach achieves English-to-French translation performance comparable to state-of-the-art phrase-based systems.

title: Sequence to Sequence Learning with Neural Networks
authors: Ilya Sutskever and Oriol Vinyals and Quoc V. Le
reason: Seminal work introducing the Seq2Seq architecture using LSTMs, marking the critical transition from SMT to neural machine translation.
summary: This paper addresses the challenge of mapping input sequences to output sequences by proposing an end-to-end architecture using a multilayered Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) encoder and decoder. On the WMT'14 English-to-French translation task, the LSTM model achieved a BLEU score of 34.8, outperforming a phrase-based statistical machine translation system's score of 33.3. When used to rerank hypotheses from the statistical system, the LSTM improved the BLEU score to 36.5.

title: Effective Approaches to Attention-based Neural Machine Translation

Their ensemble model achieved a new state-of-the-art score of 25.9 BLEU points, outperforming the previous best system by 1.0 BLEU point.

title:

summary: This paper addresses the challenge of representing linguistic phrases for statistical machine translation by proposing an RNN Encoder-Decoder model. The method uses two recurrent neural networks to encode a source sequence into a fixed-length vector and then decode it into a target sequence, training them jointly to maximize conditional probability. Integrating these learned phrase-pair probabilities as an additional feature into an existing log-linear translation model improves overall translation performance.

title: Six Challenges for Neural Machine Translation
authors: Philipp Koehn and Rebecca Knowles

summary: This paper investigates six specific limitations of neural machine translation, including domain mismatch, data scarcity, rare words, long sentences, word alignment, and beam search. title: Neural versus Phrase-Based Machine Translation Quality: a Case Study

title:

title: Improving Neural Machine Translation Models with Monolingual Data
authors: Rico Sennrich and Barry Haddow and Alexandra Birch

The resulting models achieved state-of-the-art performance, including a 4.9% accuracy increase on XNLI and a 9 BLEU improvement in unsupervised German-English translation.

title: Unsupervised Neural Machine Translation

The system achieved 15.56 BLEU points for French-to-English and 10.21 BLEU points for German-to-English translation on the WMT 2014 benchmark.

title:

authors:

title: Sequence-Level Knowledge Distillation
authors: Yoon Kim, Alexander M. Rush

title:

title: Modeling Coverage for Neural Machine Translation

title: Dual Learning for Machine Translation

title: On Using Monolingual Corpora in Neural Machine Translation
authors:

title: Scaling Neural Machine Translation

title: On Using Very Large Target Vocabulary for Neural Machine Translation

This approach achieved state-of-the-art BLEU scores for English-to-German translation and nearly state-of-the-art performance for English-to-French.

title: Addressing the Rare Word Problem in Neural Machine Translation
